title: Toeplitz Matrix Problem

content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

content.problemStatement:
With an `m x n` `matrix`, output *`true` if the matrix is Toeplitz. Otherwise, output `false`.*

A matrix is **Toeplitz** if every diagonal from top-left to bottom-right has the same elements.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/11/04/ex1.jpg)

```
Input: matrix = [[1,2,3,4],[5,1,2,3],[9,5,1,2]]
Output: true
Explanation:
In the above grid, the diagonals are:
"[9]", "[5, 5]", "[1, 1, 1]", "[2, 2, 2]", "[3, 3]", "[4]".
In each diagonal all elements are the same, so the answer is True.
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/11/04/ex2.jpg)

```
Input: matrix = [[1,2],[2,2]]
Output: false
Explanation:
The diagonal "[1, 2]" has different elements.
```

**Constraints:**

* `m == matrix.length`
* `n == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 20`
* `0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 99`

**Follow up:**

* What if the `matrix` is stored on disk, and the memory is limited such that you can only load no more than one row of the matrix into the memory at once?
* What if the `matrix` is so large that you can only load up a partial row into the memory at once?

notes: The input is already available as a matrix, so the algorithm checks each relevant pair once and returns immediately on the first mismatch.
solution.approach: For every cell that is not in the first row or first column, compare it with the cell one row up and one column left. These two cells lie on the same top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal, so equality for every such pair is exactly the Toeplitz condition.

better.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
better.description: Remove the extra diagonal storage by observing that adjacent cells on the same diagonal must be equal. Compare matrix[i][j] with matrix[i-1][j-1] for every i >= 1 and j >= 1, returning false on the first mismatch.

optimal.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Scan the matrix once from row 1 and column 1. The equality matrix[i][j] == matrix[i-1][j-1] enforces every diagonal invariant, and every required adjacent pair is checked exactly once. No additional data structure is needed.

bruteForce.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(m + n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Treat each top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal independently. Use a dictionary keyed by r-c to remember the first value seen on each diagonal, then verify every later value on that diagonal matches it. This directly follows the definition but stores one value for every diagonal.

followUps: How would you process the matrix when only one complete row can be held in memory at a time?
How would the approach change if only a partial row can be loaded at a time?
Can you stream the matrix row by row while preserving the same correctness guarantee?
